affordance_in_statement: The interlock acts as a fail-safe that strictly forbids the panel from being configured in the one specific way where both involved switches are simultaneously set to the exact opposite of their designated safe modes.
removal_suggestion: Instead of defining the rule as 'cannot both be the opposite of safe mode' (which models instantly convert to the standard CNF clause (l1 OR l2)), present the interlock as an implication or conditional constraint (e.g. 'if switch A is in state S, switch B is forced to state T') without using the word 'safe mode' or the simultaneous double-negation that identically matches DIMACS CNF semantics.

regression_risk: glm-5 already had buggy 2-SAT indexing logic; clarifying or changing the implication structure might help it fix its graph construction.
